title: How will it be when the angels come for them?
subtitle: The moment of death for those who turned back

row.title: a gentle end
sub: what I can still work for

then: After describing the hypocrites' secret deals, the verse asks a sober question. Ibn Kathir says {trap}their souls cling to their bodies, so the angels draw them out with force.{/trap} {idea}It is a reminder of how a life of double-dealing ends.{/idea}
now: Nobody chooses the day. It may be a hospital bed or a roadside. {idea}The only thing you shape is the person you are when it comes.{/idea} {reward}A heart at peace with Allah does not need to cling.{/reward}
old: I do not need to think about death until I am old.
new: How I live now shapes how I will meet the angels at the end.
try: Ask Allah today for a good ending, in your own words, once.

title: They chased what angers Him and disliked what pleases Him.
subtitle: The reason behind the hard ending
then: The verse explains the end described before it. {trap}They pursued what angered Allah and disliked what earns His pleasure, so He made their deeds worthless.{/trap} {idea}What a person loves and hates sets their direction.{/idea}
now: You notice you are bored by anything about Allah but alert for anything that pulls you away from Him. {idea}Desires have a direction.{/idea} {reward}You can ask Allah to turn your likes toward what pleases Him.{/reward}
old: What I like and dislike is just my personality.
new: My likes and dislikes point me toward or away from Allah's pleasure.
try: Make the dua: O Allah, make me love what You love. Say it three times today.

title: Did they think their hidden hatred would never show?
subtitle: What the heart hides comes out
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites thought their ill-will would stay hidden. Allah later exposed their practices in Surah at-Tawbah, which is also called the Exposer. {idea}Uthman bin Affan said no one hides a secret but Allah shows it on his face and in slips of his tongue.{/idea}
now: You smile at your colleague's promotion while resenting it. It leaks out: a sharp comment, a pause too long. {trap}Envy rarely stays quiet.{/trap} {idea}Better to treat it than to hide it.{/idea}
old: If I keep my resentment private, it hurts no one.
new: Hidden ill-will tends to show, so I should heal it, not hide it.
try: Think of someone you quietly envy. Make a sincere dua for their good today.

title: You will know them by the tone of their speech.
subtitle: Allah conceals, but words reveal
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ He could have shown him every hypocrite by name. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah did not, but conceals His creation, deals with them by what appears, and leaves inner secrets to Himself.{/idea} {trap}Still, their words reveal them.{/trap} And Allah knows all your deeds.
now: It is tempting to judge who at the mosque is sincere and who is not. {idea}The verse shows Allah's way: cover, go by what is visible, leave hearts to Him.{/idea} {reward}Then check your own tone, because Allah knows your deeds too.{/reward}
old: I can usually tell who is fake and should call them out.
new: Allah covers people, so I go by what I see and watch my own words.
try: Listen to your own tone in one conversation today. Does it match what you mean?

title: Tested until the striving and the patient are shown.
subtitle: Tests make the hidden visible
then: Allah says He will test the believers with commands and prohibitions. Ibn Kathir stresses {idea}His knowledge comes before every event{/idea}; Ibn Abbas said until We know means so that We may see. {reward}The tests make the striving and patient visible.{/reward}
now: The year with no job offers. The child who is always sick. The marriage going through a rough patch. {idea}It is not that Allah needs to find out who you are.{/idea} {reward}The test brings out your patience so it is seen and rewarded.{/reward}
old: If I am being tested, Allah must doubt me.
new: Tests bring out my striving and patience so they can be seen and rewarded.
try: Name your current test and say: this is where my patience gets shown. Then do one patient act.

title: Opposing the truth harms only yourself, never Allah.
subtitle: Turning back after guidance was clear
then: Ibn Kathir says those who opposed the Messenger ﷺ after guidance was clear {idea}could never harm Allah in the least; they only harmed themselves.{/idea} {trap}Even good they did before turning back would bring them no reward.{/trap}
now: You argue with a truth because it is inconvenient: you mock it, block it, refuse it. {idea}The truth does not shrink.{/idea} {trap}The only thing that shrinks is what you gain from it.{/trap}
old: If I push back hard enough, I can make the truth go away.
new: Fighting the truth cannot harm Allah; it only costs me.
try: Think of one truth you resist. Stop arguing with it for one day and see what changes.

title: Obey, and do not cancel out your own deeds.
subtitle: The verse that made the Companions careful
then: Ibn Umar said the Companions {trap}used to think all good deeds would be accepted{/trap} until this was revealed. They began to fear that some sins could cancel deeds. Later, after verse 4:48, {idea}they kept fearing for those who committed great sins and hoping for those who did not.{/idea}
now: You worked hard all Ramadan, then spent the next month on backbiting and anger. {idea}Good deeds are like savings: you can earn them, and you can also spend them away.{/idea} {reward}Guard what you built.{/reward}
old: Once I have done good deeds, they are safe forever.
new: My deeds are worth guarding, so I keep both fear and hope.
try: Pick one good deed you are proud of. Protect it today by avoiding one habit that undoes it.

title: Dying on rejection closes the door to forgiveness.
subtitle: The one thing that ends hope
then: Ibn Kathir links this verse to 4:48, that Allah does not forgive joining partners with Him. {trap}The key word is died: they died as disbelievers.{/trap} {reward}While a person is alive, the way back stays open.{/reward}
now: You think it is too late for you, or for someone you love who has strayed. {reward}The verse quietly says the opposite: while there is breath, the door is open.{/reward} {idea}The only deadline is the last one.{/idea}
old: Some people, maybe me, are too far gone to come back.
new: As long as I am alive, the way back to Allah is open.
try: Make a dua today for someone you have given up on, that Allah guides them.

title: Do not lose heart: Allah is with you.
subtitle: Strength for a small, pressed community
then: Ibn Kathir says this tells the believers not to be weak and seek a truce out of fear while they hold the upper hand. He notes that when it served the Muslims, {idea}the Prophet ﷺ accepted a ten-year treaty after being blocked from Makkah.{/idea} {reward}Allah is with you and will never reduce your deeds.{/reward}
now: You are close to finishing the degree, the memorization, the long repair of a friendship, and you want to quit. {idea}Not every pause is weakness, but quitting from fear when you can carry on often is.{/idea} {reward}Allah is with you, and no effort is lost.{/reward}
old: When it gets hard, it is easier to just give up.
new: With Allah with me, I do not need to give up from fear, and none of my effort is lost.
try: Do one more small step today on something you have been tempted to abandon.

title: This life is play, and He does not ask all you own.
subtitle: What lasts, and what is actually asked
then: Ibn Kathir says this life is only play, except what is done for Allah. {idea}He needs nothing from you.{/idea} {reward}He asked for charity so you would help your needy brothers, and its benefit and reward come back to you.{/reward}
now: Your weekend disappears into scrolling and shopping, and on Monday you cannot remember any of it. {idea}That is the play and distraction.{/idea} {reward}The hour you spent helping a neighbor move is the part that stays.{/reward}
old: Giving charity is a cost that takes from me.
new: Allah does not need my money; giving helps others and comes back to me.
try: Give a small amount to someone in need today, and notice how it feels.

title: If He pressed you for everything, you would hold back.
subtitle: Allah knows how attached we are to money
then: Ibn Kathir quotes Qatadah: {idea}Allah knows that taking people's money brings out ill-will.{/idea} He adds that Qatadah was right, {trap}because money is dear to people, and they only spend it on what is dearer to them.{/trap} So Allah asks for a part, not all.
now: Someone asks to borrow a large sum and you feel a tightness in your chest. {idea}That tightness is human, and Allah knows it.{/idea} {reward}It is why He asks for a portion, not everything.{/reward}
old: I would give anything for Allah if He asked.
new: Allah knows how much I cling to money, so He asks only a portion with mercy.
try: Notice the tight feeling the next time you spend on someone else, and give anyway.

title: Whoever holds back is only holding back from himself.
subtitle: Allah is free of need, and we are the needy
then: The believers were invited to spend in Allah's cause, and some held back. Ibn Kathir says {trap}the stingy person only reduces his own reward.{/trap} {idea}Allah needs nothing, while everything needs Him.{/idea} If they turned away, He would bring people who would obey.
now: A fundraiser link sits unopened in your messages. You tell yourself someone else will cover it. {idea}Someone probably will.{/idea} {trap}The only one who loses out is you.{/trap}
old: If I do not give, the cause loses out.
new: Allah's work will go on; if I hold back, I am the one who loses.
try: Open one charity request you have been ignoring and give something, however small.
